refuter_findings.evidence: The Statement claims tangent space “ker d_1 / im d_0 for the infinitesimal ADHM deformation maps” but does not define those maps. Its tangent-space dependency states only the generic isomorphism T_xM/T_x(G·x) ≅ T_[x](M/G); the raw ADHM definition supplies no d_0 or d_1. Their formulas first appear in Proof step 2.1, which does not define the Statement’s notation at its use.

The proof asserts, “On P², an effective divisor has nonnegative intersection degree with L_infty,” without applying an intersection result. The opened intersection supplier gives C·D = deg_C(O_X(D)|_C), while the opened Bézout supplier applies only to plane curves with no common component. The proof does not decompose the divisor, apply Bézout to components distinct from L_infty, or compute L_infty² = 1 for a component equal to L_infty.

Step 6.1 tensors the diagonal Koszul resolution by E(-1), and step 7.1 tensors it by the family E. The cited Koszul supplier says “Tensoring with a vector bundle preserves it”; here E is only torsion-free, and the family hypothesis is flatness over S. The proof does not establish exactness after this tensor operation, for example by showing the diagonal is flat over the first projection or checking the coordinate-difference sequence on the pulled-back sheaf.

The proof says a nonzero finite-length torsion submodule “would force depth zero,” but the Auslander–Buchsbaum supplier gives the formula pd_R(M) + depth_R(M) = depth(R), not this implication. A nonzero finite-length submodule has a nonzero socle element, giving a nonzero map from the residue field and hence depth zero; that step is not supplied or derived.

For a finite-type family the proof asserts that 0 → V O(-1) → K → E → 0 is exact, then establishes injectivity only after restriction to each residue field, citing step 1.1, which treats fixed complex data. Fiberwise sheaf-injectivity does not itself establish injectivity of the total-space map over the base. The proof gives no relative exactness argument, such as the local monic-block determinant argument available for this matrix.

refuter_findings.evidence: [F6] asserts that two commuting endomorphisms of a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space have a common eigenvector, but cites only the supplier whose Statement is “The field C is algebraically closed.” That statement supplies eigenvalues, not the simultaneous-eigenvector implication. The proof omits the short derivation using an eigenspace of the first map, its invariance under the second, and an eigenvector of the restriction.

reader_findings.evidence: The statement asserts the quotient tangent space is ker d_1 / im d_0 but defines neither map there or in an earlier supplier. Their formulas and domains first appear in Proof step 2.1. Include the maps in the statement or identify an exact earlier definition and its relevant content.

reader_findings.location: Facts & Assumptions preamble and Proof step 2.1 (item lines 89 and 121)
reader_findings.evidence: The slope argument uses nonnegative intersection degree of an effective divisor with L_infty. The item asserts this but does not apply an exact intersection result. The A-page has an intersection-theory page prerequisite, but the proof should spell out the application: use Bezout for components other than L_infty and compute L_infty squared as 1 for a component equal to L_infty, then add with multiplicity.

The proof tensors the diagonal Koszul resolution by E(-1), and later by an S-flat family whose fibers are only torsion-free. The cited Koszul supplier establishes the diagonal resolution and tensor exactness for a vector bundle; it does not establish exactness after tensoring by this non-locally-free sheaf. Prove relative purity, for example from flatness of the diagonal over the first projection and flatness of the Koszul terms, or give a local coordinate-difference argument before using the spectral sequence.

The proof excludes finite-length torsion by asserting that a nonzero finite-length submodule forces depth zero, but supplies no argument or exact supplier for this fact. A nonzero socle element gives a nonzero map from the residue field and hence depth zero.

The proof concludes T_P2(-3) is stable of slope -3/2 without computing its degree from the Euler sequence. Also, stability controls only rank-one proper subsheaves, while the image of E to T_P2(-3) can have rank two. Compute deg T_P2(-3) = -3 and apply the full-rank subsheaf bound from step 2.1, as well as the rank-one stability bound, to justify the claimed contradiction.

For an arbitrary finite-type ADHM data family, the proof asserts 0 -> V O(-1) -> K -> E -> 0 is exact after citing only the fiberwise monad result. Total-space injectivity of alpha is needed before the residue-field Tor and flatness arguments, but is not established. Prove it locally from the explicit matrix, for example using an appropriate monic block determinant on each standard chart, or cite and verify a relative exactness criterion.

reader_findings.evidence: The common-eigenvector fact for two commuting endomorphisms is attributed only to the supplier that states C is algebraically closed. The needed implication is not in that supplier statement. Derive it by taking an eigenspace of the first map, using commutativity to show it is invariant under the second, then taking an eigenvector of the restriction.
